violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: sliced tomato at 58F, sliced Provolone cheese at 60F in 2 DR prep cooler at kitchen (61F).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC relocated sliced tomato and sliced Provolone cheese that had been in the cooler for less than four hours.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 2 DR prep cooler at 61F.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC agreed to discontinue use of unit. PIC contacted technician during inspection.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The sink basin at the kitchen is slow to drain.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. EHS discussed with PIC repairing the sink drain/plumbing to ensure proper drainage

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Parasite Destruction
violations.observation: The following fish offered for service or sale in the ready-to-eat form was not frozen to ensure parasite destruction: Observed that the parasite destruction letter for tilapia (Ceviche) is missing.
violations.corrective_action: Before service or sale in ready-to-eat form, raw or partially cooked fish shall be: 1) frozen and stored at a temperature of -4F or below for a minimum of 7 days in a freezer, or 2) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -31F or below for a minimum of 15 hours, or 3) frozen at -31F or below until solid and stored at -4F or below for a minimum of 24 hours. PIC contacted the supplier and obtained the parasite destruction letter during the inspection

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: Observed that reminder and disclosure for ceviche (raw tilapia) are missing on the menu.
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. PIC updated the menu with reminder and disclosure for ceviche during the inspection.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. EHS provided a copy of vomit and diarrheal instruction. PIC posted vomit and diarrhea instruction in conspicuous place.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: Observed raw tilapia in unopened vacuum packaging sitting in ambient water on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC removed the vacuum-packaged tilapia from water, opened the vacuum packaging, and moved it to WIC for proper thawing. CHICKEN RICO (Inspection Date: 04/16/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. Observed wet wiping cloths on prep table.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC placed wiping cloth in sanitizer solution.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED COLESLAW AT 50F AND SALAD AT 46F IN SERVICE-LINE COLD HOLDING AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC AGREED TO PUT FOOD ITEMS ON TIME. PIC UNDERSTANDS TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL SHOULD BE PROPERLY USED (START AT 41F OR BELOW, WITH 4-HOUR TIME MARKING) OR THE FACILITY MUST ENSURE THAT THE FOODS HERE STAY AT 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: OBSERVED COMMERCIALLY PACKAGED TILAPIA IN INTACT VACUUM PACKAGING, THAWING IN WALK-IN COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: PIC SLIT OPEN PACKAGING FOR THAWING TILAPIA DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAWING VACUUM PACKAGED FISH SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM THE PACKAGING, OR THE PACKAGE SHOULD BE SLIT OPEN WHEN THE THAWING PROCESS BEGINS.
